items.explanation: Distribute: $8x - 6 - 3x - -9 = -12$. Combine like terms: $5x + 3 = -12$, so $x = -3$.
items.skill_note: The minus sign in front of the second parenthesis flips every sign inside it.

items.stem: If $\frac{2x + 4}{2} = 3$, what is the value of $x$?
choice_notes: multiplied by $2$ but never divided by $2$
added $4$ instead of subtracting it
sign error while isolating $x$
correct
items.explanation: Multiply both sides by $2$: $2x + 4 = 6$. Then $2x = 2$, so $x = 1$.
items.skill_note: Clear the denominator before moving the constant; the coefficient $a$ still has to be divided out.

items.stem: If $\frac{6x + 6}{2} = -6$, what is the value of $x$?
choice_notes: added $6$ instead of subtracting it
sign error while isolating $x$
correct
multiplied by $2$ only on the numerator's variable term
items.explanation: Multiply both sides by $2$: $6x + 6 = -12$. Then $6x = -18$, so $x = -3$.
items.skill_note: Clear the denominator before moving the constant; the coefficient $a$ still has to be divided out.

items.stem: If $\frac{4x + 8}{2} = 6$, what is the value of $x$?
items.explanation: Multiply both sides by $2$: $4x + 8 = 12$. Then $4x = 4$, so $x = 1$.
items.skill_note: Clear the denominator before moving the constant; the coefficient $a$ still has to be divided out.

items.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ that satisfy $-6x - 8 < 3x + 19$?
choice_notes: left the boundary in even though the inequality is strict
correct
divided by $-9$ without reversing the inequality
changed the sign of the boundary instead of the direction
items.explanation: Subtract $3x$ from both sides: $-9x - 8 < 19$. Then $-9x < 27$, and dividing by $-9$ reverses the symbol: $x > -3$.
items.skill_note: When both sides hold $x$, combine first; the flip happens exactly once, at the final division by a negative.

items.stem: What is the smallest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $-2x + 4 < x + 22$?
items.explanation: Collect $x$ on the left: $-3x < 18$, so $x > -6$ after dividing by a negative. The smallest integer greater than $-6$ is $-5$.
items.skill_note: Move the smaller $x$-term to keep the coefficient positive when you can; otherwise remember the flip.

items.stem: What is the smallest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $-4x + 7 < 2x - 5$?
items.explanation: Collect $x$ on the left: $-6x < -12$, so $x > 2$ after dividing by a negative. The smallest integer greater than $2$ is $3$.
items.skill_note: Move the smaller $x$-term to keep the coefficient positive when you can; otherwise remember the flip.

items.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ that satisfy $-20 < 2x - 6 < -10$?
choice_notes: used non-strict symbols even though both ends are strict
described the outside of the interval instead of the inside
negated both endpoints instead of dividing by $2$
correct
items.explanation: Subtract $-6$ from all three parts: $-14 < 2x < -4$. Divide by $2$: $-7 < x < -2$.
items.skill_note: A compound inequality stays compound; the trap is turning the interval inside-out into two rays.

items.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ that satisfy $2 < 3x + 2 < 17$?
choice_notes: used non-strict symbols even though both ends are strict
negated both endpoints instead of dividing by $3$
correct
described the outside of the interval instead of the inside
items.explanation: Subtract $2$ from all three parts: $0 < 3x < 15$. Divide by $3$: $0 < x < 5$.
items.skill_note: A compound inequality stays compound; the trap is turning the interval inside-out into two rays.

items.stem: How many integer values of $x$ satisfy $-9 < 4x + 3 < 19$?
items.explanation: Subtract $3$ throughout: $-12 < 4x < 16$. Divide by $4$: $-3 < x < 4$. The integers strictly between $-3$ and $4$ are $-2$ through $3$, which is $6$ values.
items.skill_note: Apply the same operation to all three parts; count integers strictly between the endpoints.

items.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ that satisfy $3 < 2x + 3 < 19$?
choice_notes: negated both endpoints instead of dividing by $2$
used non-strict symbols even though both ends are strict
described the outside of the interval instead of the inside
correct
items.explanation: Subtract $3$ from all three parts: $0 < 2x < 16$. Divide by $2$: $0 < x < 8$.
items.skill_note: A compound inequality stays compound; the trap is turning the interval inside-out into two rays.

items.stem: What is the sum of all solutions to $|3x - 6| = 9$?
choice_notes: subtracted the two solutions instead of adding
dropped the sign of the sum
gave only the positive solution
correct
items.explanation: Split into two cases: $3x - 6 = 9$ gives $x = 5$, and $3x - 6 = -9$ gives $x = -1$. Their sum is $-1 + 5 = 4$.
items.skill_note: An absolute value equation produces two cases; forgetting the negative case loses a solution.

items.stem: What is the sum of all solutions to $|5x - 25| = 15$?
items.explanation: Split into two cases: $5x - 25 = 15$ gives $x = 8$, and $5x - 25 = -15$ gives $x = 2$. Their sum is $2 + 8 = 10$.
items.skill_note: An absolute value equation produces two cases; forgetting the negative case loses a solution.

items.stem: What is the sum of all solutions to $|2x - 2| = 4$?
items.explanation: Split into two cases: $2x - 2 = 4$ gives $x = 3$, and $2x - 2 = -4$ gives $x = -1$. Their sum is $-1 + 3 = 2$.
items.skill_note: An absolute value equation produces two cases; forgetting the negative case loses a solution.

items.stem: What is the greater solution to $|2x - 8| = 4$?
choice_notes: divided by $2$ before clearing the absolute value
correct
gave the lesser solution
gave the sum of the solutions
items.explanation: Split into two cases: $2x - 8 = 4$ gives $x = 6$, and $2x - 8 = -4$ gives $x = 2$. The greater of the two is $6$.
items.skill_note: An absolute value equation produces two cases; forgetting the negative case loses a solution.

items.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ that satisfy $|4x + 16| < 12$?
choice_notes: used the "greater than" pattern for a "less than" inequality
divided by $4$ without also dividing the endpoints
correct
kept the endpoints although the inequality is strict
items.explanation: The inequality $|u| < 12$ means $-12 < u < 12$, so $-12 < 4x + 16 < 12$. Subtract $16$ and divide by $4$ to get $-7 < x < -1$.
items.skill_note: "Less than" gives a bounded interval; the endpoints are excluded because the symbol is strict.

items.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ that satisfy $|3x - 15| < 6$?
choice_notes: used the "greater than" pattern for a "less than" inequality
divided by $3$ without also dividing the endpoints
kept the endpoints although the inequality is strict
correct
items.explanation: The inequality $|u| < 6$ means $-6 < u < 6$, so $-6 < 3x - 15 < 6$. Subtract $-15$ and divide by $3$ to get $3 < x < 7$.
items.skill_note: "Less than" gives a bounded interval; the endpoints are excluded because the symbol is strict.

items.stem: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $|2x - 8| < 10$?
items.explanation: Rewrite as $-10 < 2x - 8 < 10$, so $-1 < x < 9$. The greatest integer strictly less than $9$ is $8$.
items.skill_note: A "less than" absolute value becomes a single interval between two endpoints.

items.stem: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $|2x - 8| < 8$?
items.explanation: Rewrite as $-8 < 2x - 8 < 8$, so $0 < x < 8$. The greatest integer strictly less than $8$ is $7$.
items.skill_note: A "less than" absolute value becomes a single interval between two endpoints.

items.stem: The line passing through $(-4, 7)$ and $(-2, k)$ has slope $-0.5$. What is the value of $k$?
items.explanation: The rise is $k - 7 = -0.5(-2 - (-4)) = -1$, so $k = 7 - 1 = 6$. Each unit of horizontal change moves $y$ by $-0.5$.
items.skill_note: Slope times horizontal change gives the rise, which then has to be added to the known $y$-value.

items.stem: The line passing through $(-6, -7)$ and $(-1, k)$ has slope $2$. What is the value of $k$?
choice_notes: correct
subtracted the rise instead of adding it
added the slope times $x_2$ to $y_1$ instead of the horizontal change
forgot to add the starting $y$-value
items.explanation: The rise is $k - (-7) = 2(-1 - (-6)) = 10$, so $k = -7 + 10 = 3$. Each unit of horizontal change moves $y$ by $2$.
items.skill_note: Slope times horizontal change gives the rise, which then has to be added to the known $y$-value.

items.stem: The line passing through $(1, -5)$ and $(7, k)$ has slope $0.5$. What is the value of $k$?
choice_notes: added the $x$-coordinates instead of subtracting
subtracted the rise instead of adding it
correct
forgot to add the starting $y$-value
items.explanation: The rise is $k - (-5) = 0.5(7 - 1) = 3$, so $k = -5 + 3 = -2$. Each unit of horizontal change moves $y$ by $0.5$.
items.skill_note: Slope times horizontal change gives the rise, which then has to be added to the known $y$-value.

items.stem: In the system of equations $2x+ky=9$ and $4x+(k+3)y=18$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of $k$?
choice_notes: correct
halved the $y$-coefficient instead of matching the ratio
used the constant ratio backwards
made the coefficients negatives of each other
items.explanation: Infinitely many solutions requires the second equation to be the first multiplied by a constant. The $x$-coefficients give the factor $\frac{4}{2}=2$, and the constants agree because $18=2(9)$. So the $y$-coefficients must also satisfy $(k+3)=2k$, giving $k=3$.
items.skill_note: Check all three ratios — coefficients and constants. If only the coefficients match, the lines are parallel (no solution) instead.

items.stem: A community pool charges a membership fee of $40$ dollars plus $4$ dollars for each visit. The total cost $C$, in dollars, for $x$ visits is given by $C = 4x + 40$. What does $4$ represent in this model?
choices: the cost of each additional visit
the number of visits that cost $40$ dollars
choice_notes: multiplied the coefficient by itself instead of interpreting it as a rate
correct
treated the coefficient as a count rather than a rate
described the constant term instead of the coefficient
items.explanation: The coefficient of $x$ is the rate of change: each additional visit raises the cost by $4$ dollars. The constant $40$ is the membership fee, charged even when $x = 0$.
items.skill_note: In $C = mx + b$, the coefficient of $x$ is the per-unit rate and the constant is the starting amount.

items.stem: A gym charges a one-time registration fee of $18$ dollars plus $4$ dollars for each class attended. The total cost $C$, in dollars, for $x$ classs is given by $C = 4x + 18$. What does $4$ represent in this model?
choices: the number of classs that cost $18$ dollars
the cost of each additional class
choice_notes: treated the coefficient as a count rather than a rate
multiplied the coefficient by itself instead of interpreting it as a rate
described the constant term instead of the coefficient
correct
items.explanation: The coefficient of $x$ is the rate of change: each additional class raises the cost by $4$ dollars. The constant $18$ is the registration fee, charged even when $x = 0$.
items.skill_note: In $C = mx + b$, the coefficient of $x$ is the per-unit rate and the constant is the starting amount.

items.stem: A cell phone plan charges a flat monthly fee of $20$ dollars plus $2$ dollars for each gigabyte of data used. The total cost $C$, in dollars, for $x$ gigabytes is given by $C = 2x + 20$. What does $2$ represent in this model?
choices: the cost of each additional gigabyte
the number of gigabytes that cost $20$ dollars
choice_notes: correct
described the constant term instead of the coefficient
multiplied the coefficient by itself instead of interpreting it as a rate
treated the coefficient as a count rather than a rate
items.explanation: The coefficient of $x$ is the rate of change: each additional gigabyte raises the cost by $2$ dollars. The constant $20$ is the monthly fee, charged even when $x = 0$.
items.skill_note: In $C = mx + b$, the coefficient of $x$ is the per-unit rate and the constant is the starting amount.

items.skill: Linear models from two data points
items.stem: A print shop charges a fixed setup fee plus a constant price per page. Printing $5$ pages costs $30$ dollars, and printing $9$ pages costs $46$ dollars. What is the charge, in dollars, for printing $12$ pages?
choice_notes: doubled the time interval instead of extending by $3$
used $y = mx + b$ with $b = y_1$ instead of finding the intercept
correct
moved in the wrong direction from the first data point
items.explanation: The rate is $\frac{46 - 30}{9 - 5} = 4$ dollars per unit time. From the first point, the value at time $t$ is $30 + 4 (t - 5)$. At $t = 12$ this is $30 + 28 = 58$.
items.skill_note: Extend the pattern by multiplying the rate by the change in the input, not by adding the input difference.

items.skill: Linear models from two data points
items.stem: A hiker is walking toward a lookout point at a steady pace. She is $45$ kilometers from the lookout after $2$ hours and $60$ kilometers from it after $5$ hours. How many kilometers from the lookout is she after $9$ hours?
items.explanation: The rate is $\frac{60 - 45}{5 - 2} = 5$ kilometers per unit time. From the first point, the value at time $t$ is $45 + 5 (t - 2)$. At $t = 9$ this is $45 + 35 = 80$.
items.skill_note: Extend the pattern by multiplying the rate by the change in the input, not by adding the input difference.

items.skill: Linear models from two data points
items.stem: A hiker is walking toward a lookout point at a steady pace. She is $60$ kilometers from the lookout after $3$ hours and $64$ kilometers from it after $5$ hours. How many kilometers from the lookout is she after $9$ hours?
items.explanation: The rate is $\frac{64 - 60}{5 - 3} = 2$ kilometers per unit time. From the first point, the value at time $t$ is $60 + 2 (t - 3)$. At $t = 9$ this is $60 + 12 = 72$.
items.skill_note: Extend the pattern by multiplying the rate by the change in the input, not by adding the input difference.

items.stem: Which equation represents the line that passes through $(-3, 1)$ and $(-1, 5)$?
choice_notes: swapped the slope and the intercept
correct
used $y_1$ as the intercept without adjusting for the slope
computed the slope with the coordinates in inconsistent order
items.explanation: Slope $= \frac{5 - 1}{-1 - -3} = 2$. Then $2(-3) + 7 = 1$, so the intercept is $7$ and $y = 2x + 7$.
items.skill_note: Finding the slope is only half the job; the intercept must be recomputed, not copied from a data point.

items.stem: Which equation represents the line that passes through $(0, 2)$ and $(1, 3.5)$?
choice_notes: computed the slope with the coordinates in inconsistent order
correct
swapped the slope and the intercept
used $y_1$ as the intercept without adjusting for the slope
items.explanation: Slope $= \frac{3.5 - 2}{1 - 0} = 1.5$. Then $1.5(0) + 2 = 2$, so the intercept is $2$ and $y = 1.5x + 2$.
items.skill_note: Finding the slope is only half the job; the intercept must be recomputed, not copied from a data point.

items.stem: Which equation represents the line that passes through $(-5, 4)$ and $(0, -11)$?
choice_notes: computed the slope with the coordinates in inconsistent order
used $y_1$ as the intercept without adjusting for the slope
swapped the slope and the intercept
correct
items.explanation: Slope $= \frac{-11 - 4}{0 - -5} = -3$. Then $-3(-5) - 11 = 4$, so the intercept is $-11$ and $y = -3x - 11$.
items.skill_note: Finding the slope is only half the job; the intercept must be recomputed, not copied from a data point.

items.stem: Which equation represents the line that passes through $(-5, 6)$ and $(-1, -6)$?
choice_notes: swapped the slope and the intercept
computed the slope with the coordinates in inconsistent order
correct
used $y_1$ as the intercept without adjusting for the slope
items.explanation: Slope $= \frac{-6 - 6}{-1 - -5} = -3$. Then $-3(-5) - 9 = 6$, so the intercept is $-9$ and $y = -3x - 9$.
items.skill_note: Finding the slope is only half the job; the intercept must be recomputed, not copied from a data point.

items.stem: The line $\ell$ is parallel to $6x + 24y = 9$ and passes through $(3, 3)$. What is the $y$-intercept of $\ell$?
choice_notes: added the slope times the $x$-coordinate instead of subtracting it
correct
used the perpendicular slope instead of the parallel slope
assumed a parallel line must have the same intercept
items.explanation: The given line has slope $-0.25$. A parallel line shares that slope, so $-0.25(3) + 3.75 = 3$, giving $b = 3.75$.
items.skill_note: Parallel lines share a slope but not an intercept; substitute the point to find the new intercept.

items.stem: The line $\ell$ is parallel to $6x + 6y = 12$ and passes through $(2, 8)$. What is the $y$-intercept of $\ell$?
choice_notes: used the perpendicular slope instead of the parallel slope
correct
added the slope times the $x$-coordinate instead of subtracting it
assumed a parallel line must have the same intercept
items.explanation: The given line has slope $-1$. A parallel line shares that slope, so $-1(2) + 10 = 8$, giving $b = 10$.
items.skill_note: Parallel lines share a slope but not an intercept; substitute the point to find the new intercept.

items.stem: The line $\ell$ is parallel to $6x + 18y = 20$ and passes through $(3, 7)$. What is the $y$-intercept of $\ell$?
choice_notes: added the slope times the $x$-coordinate instead of subtracting it
used the perpendicular slope instead of the parallel slope
assumed a parallel line must have the same intercept
correct
items.explanation: The given line has slope $-0.33$. A parallel line shares that slope, so $-0.33(3) + 8 = 7$, giving $b = 8$.
items.skill_note: Parallel lines share a slope but not an intercept; substitute the point to find the new intercept.

items.stem: The line $\ell$ is parallel to $4x + 8y = 17$ and passes through $(4, 1)$. What is the $y$-intercept of $\ell$?
choice_notes: assumed a parallel line must have the same intercept
correct
added the slope times the $x$-coordinate instead of subtracting it
used the perpendicular slope instead of the parallel slope
items.explanation: The given line has slope $-0.5$. A parallel line shares that slope, so $-0.5(4) + 3 = 1$, giving $b = 3$.
items.skill_note: Parallel lines share a slope but not an intercept; substitute the point to find the new intercept.

items.stem: If $x + y = -4$ and $6x + 3y = -6$, what is the value of $x$?
choice_notes: added the products instead of subtracting in the numerator
made a sign error during elimination
correct
solved for the other variable
items.explanation: Elimination: multiply the first equation by $6$ and the second by $1$, then subtract to eliminate $x$. This gives $y = -6$ and back-substitution gives $x = 2$.
items.skill_note: Elimination must scale both sides of an equation; back-substitute to recover the other variable.

items.stem: If $4x + 2y = 2$ and $2x - 4y = -14$, what is the value of $x + y$?
choice_notes: correct
added the products instead of subtracting in the numerator
made a sign error during elimination
solved for the other variable
items.explanation: Elimination: multiply the first equation by $2$ and the second by $4$, then subtract to eliminate $x$. This gives $y = 3$ and back-substitution gives $x = -1$. So $x + y = 2$.
items.skill_note: Elimination must scale both sides of an equation; back-substitute to recover the other variable.

items.stem: If $6x + 2y = 42$ and $3x + 5y = 9$, what is the value of $y$?
choice_notes: solved for the other variable
added the products instead of subtracting in the numerator
correct
made a sign error during elimination
items.explanation: Elimination: multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second by $6$, then subtract to eliminate $x$. This gives $y = -3$ and back-substitution gives $x = 8$.
items.skill_note: Elimination must scale both sides of an equation; back-substitute to recover the other variable.

items.stem: A lab technician has a solution that is $15$ percent acid and another that is $70$ percent acid. How many liters of the $15$ percent solution must be mixed with $12$ liters of the $70$ percent solution to obtain a mixture that is $30$ percent acid?
choice_notes: added the concentration difference directly to the volume
correct
used the same volume for both solutions
divided the acid amounts instead of comparing to the target concentration
items.explanation: Acid in = acid out: $15v + 70(12) = 30(v + 12)$. This gives $-15v = 40(12)$, so $v = 32$.
items.skill_note: Track the amount of pure acid, not just the volume; the concentration equation closes the system.

items.stem: A lab technician has a solution that is $25$ percent acid and another that is $40$ percent acid. How many liters of the $25$ percent solution must be mixed with $8$ liters of the $40$ percent solution to obtain a mixture that is $30$ percent acid?
choice_notes: correct
added the concentration difference directly to the volume
divided the acid amounts instead of comparing to the target concentration
used the same volume for both solutions
items.explanation: Acid in = acid out: $25v + 40(8) = 30(v + 8)$. This gives $-5v = 10(8)$, so $v = 16$.
items.skill_note: Track the amount of pure acid, not just the volume; the concentration equation closes the system.

items.stem: Two technicians worked a total of $16$ hours on a job and earned $288$ dollars altogether. One earns $20$ dollars per hour and the other earns $12$ dollars per hour. How many hours did the technician who earns $20$ dollars per hour work?
items.explanation: Let $h$ be the hours at $20$ dollars per hour. Then $20h + 12(16 - h) = 288$, so $8h = 96$ and $h = 12$.
items.skill_note: The two hourly rates weight the two unknown hour totals; substituting one into the other is fastest.

items.stem: Two technicians worked a total of $15$ hours on a job and earned $250$ dollars altogether. One earns $22$ dollars per hour and the other earns $14$ dollars per hour. How many hours did the technician who earns $22$ dollars per hour work?
choice_notes: split the hours evenly between the two rates
solved for the other technician's hours
made an off-by-one error after eliminating
correct
items.explanation: Let $h$ be the hours at $22$ dollars per hour. Then $22h + 14(15 - h) = 250$, so $8h = 40$ and $h = 5$.
items.skill_note: The two hourly rates weight the two unknown hour totals; substituting one into the other is fastest.

items.stem: In the system of equations $4x + 5y = 18$ and $kx + 20y = 79$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of $k$?
choice_notes: correct
matched the ratio but dropped the sign
inverted the ratio of the $y$-coefficients
divided by the multiplier instead of multiplying
items.explanation: No solution means the lines are parallel but distinct: $\frac{4}{k} = \frac{5}{20}$ with $\frac{18}{79}$ different. Cross multiplying gives $5k = 80$, so $k = 16$. The constant ratio check fails, so the lines are not the same line.
items.skill_note: No solution requires equal coefficient ratios but a different constant ratio; the parameter usually sits in one coefficient.

items.stem: In the system of equations $5x + 2y = 7$ and $kx + 4y = 10$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of $k$?
items.explanation: No solution means the lines are parallel but distinct: $\frac{5}{k} = \frac{2}{4}$ with $\frac{7}{10}$ different. Cross multiplying gives $2k = 20$, so $k = 10$. The constant ratio check fails, so the lines are not the same line.
items.skill_note: No solution requires equal coefficient ratios but a different constant ratio; the parameter usually sits in one coefficient.

items.stem: In the system of equations $5x + 2y = 17$ and $kx + 4y = 41$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of $k$?
choice_notes: correct
matched the ratio but dropped the sign
divided by the multiplier instead of multiplying
rounded the proportional coefficient up by one multiple
items.explanation: No solution means the lines are parallel but distinct: $\frac{5}{k} = \frac{2}{4}$ with $\frac{17}{41}$ different. Cross multiplying gives $2k = 20$, so $k = 10$. The constant ratio check fails, so the lines are not the same line.
items.skill_note: No solution requires equal coefficient ratios but a different constant ratio; the parameter usually sits in one coefficient.

items.stem: In the system of equations $7x + 2y = 3$ and $kx + 6y = 14$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has no solution, what is the value of $k$?
choice_notes: rounded the proportional coefficient up by one multiple
divided by the multiplier instead of multiplying
correct
matched the ratio but dropped the sign
items.explanation: No solution means the lines are parallel but distinct: $\frac{7}{k} = \frac{2}{6}$ with $\frac{3}{14}$ different. Cross multiplying gives $2k = 42$, so $k = 21$. The constant ratio check fails, so the lines are not the same line.
items.skill_note: No solution requires equal coefficient ratios but a different constant ratio; the parameter usually sits in one coefficient.

items.stem: In the system of equations $7x + 3y = 18$ and $28x + 12y = 72$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of $k$?
choice_notes: derived $k$ from the constant terms instead of the $x$-coefficients
used a different multiple than the one relating the constants
correct
matched the ratio but reversed the sign
items.explanation: Infinitely many solutions means the two equations describe the same line, so all three ratios match: $\frac{7}{28} = \frac{3}{12} = \frac{18}{72}$. The first equality gives $k = 28$, and $18(12) = 72(3)$ confirms the constants scale the same way.
items.skill_note: Infinitely many solutions requires all three ratios to match, not just the coefficients.

items.stem: In the system of equations $7x + 4y = 8$ and $28x + 16y = 32$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of $k$?
items.explanation: Infinitely many solutions means the two equations describe the same line, so all three ratios match: $\frac{7}{28} = \frac{4}{16} = \frac{8}{32}$. The first equality gives $k = 28$, and $8(16) = 32(4)$ confirms the constants scale the same way.
items.skill_note: Infinitely many solutions requires all three ratios to match, not just the coefficients.

items.stem: In the system of equations $4x + 5y = 6$ and $8x + 10y = 12$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of $k$?
items.explanation: Infinitely many solutions means the two equations describe the same line, so all three ratios match: $\frac{4}{8} = \frac{5}{10} = \frac{6}{12}$. The first equality gives $k = 8$, and $6(10) = 12(5)$ confirms the constants scale the same way.
items.skill_note: Infinitely many solutions requires all three ratios to match, not just the coefficients.

items.stem: In the system of equations $2x + 2y = 10$ and $6x + 6y = 30$, $k$ is a constant. If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of $k$?
choice_notes: correct
used a different multiple than the one relating the constants
derived $k$ from the constant terms instead of the $x$-coefficients
matched the ratio but reversed the sign
items.explanation: Infinitely many solutions means the two equations describe the same line, so all three ratios match: $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{10}{30}$. The first equality gives $k = 6$, and $10(6) = 30(2)$ confirms the constants scale the same way.
items.skill_note: Infinitely many solutions requires all three ratios to match, not just the coefficients.

items.stem: The lines $y = 3x + c$ and $y = -2x + d$ intersect at the point $(6, 10)$. What is the value of $c + d$?
items.explanation: Substitute the point into each line. From the first, $10 = 3(6) + c$, so $c = -8$. From the second, $10 = -2(6) + d$, so $d = 22$. Therefore $c + d = 14$.
items.skill_note: A point on a line satisfies its equation; each intercept is found by substituting the intersection point.

items.stem: The lines $y = 3x + c$ and $y = -3x + d$ intersect at the point $(4, 4)$. What is the value of $c + d$?
items.explanation: Substitute the point into each line. From the first, $4 = 3(4) + c$, so $c = -8$. From the second, $4 = -3(4) + d$, so $d = 16$. Therefore $c + d = 8$.
items.skill_note: A point on a line satisfies its equation; each intercept is found by substituting the intersection point.

items.stem: The lines $y = 4x + c$ and $y = -2x + d$ intersect at the point $(6, 11)$. What is the value of $c + d$?

correct
used the $y$-coordinate as the sum of the intercepts
made a sign error solving for one intercept
items.explanation: Substitute the point into each line. From the first, $11 = 4(6) + c$, so $c = -13$. From the second, $11 = -2(6) + d$, so $d = 23$. Therefore $c + d = 10$.
items.skill_note: A point on a line satisfies its equation; each intercept is found by substituting the intersection point.

items.stem: A hiking group can carry at most $94$ pounds of gear. Each tent weighs $10$ pounds and each food crate weighs $6$ pounds. If the group brings $2$ tents, what is the greatest number of food crates they can carry?
choice_notes: stopped one crate short of the maximum
ignored the weight of the tents
rounded up instead of down
correct
items.explanation: Weight used by tents is $2(10) = 20$ pounds, leaving $74$ pounds. Since each crate weighs $6$ pounds, the number of crates is $\frac{74}{6} \approx 12.33$, rounded down to $12$.
items.skill_note: A "greatest number" question needs the floor of the quotient, and every consuming item must be counted.

items.stem: A hiking group can carry at most $128$ pounds of gear. Each tent weighs $13$ pounds and each food crate weighs $6$ pounds. If the group brings $3$ tents, what is the greatest number of food crates they can carry?
choice_notes: rounded up instead of down
correct

stopped one crate short of the maximum
items.explanation: Weight used by tents is $3(13) = 39$ pounds, leaving $89$ pounds. Since each crate weighs $6$ pounds, the number of crates is $\frac{89}{6} \approx 14.83$, rounded down to $14$.
items.skill_note: A "greatest number" question needs the floor of the quotient, and every consuming item must be counted.

items.stem: A hiking group can carry at most $84$ pounds of gear. Each tent weighs $9$ pounds and each food crate weighs $7$ pounds. If the group brings $2$ tents, what is the greatest number of food crates they can carry?

items.stem: A hiking group can carry at most $67$ pounds of gear. Each tent weighs $8$ pounds and each food crate weighs $8$ pounds. If the group brings $1$ tents, what is the greatest number of food crates they can carry?

items.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = 4x + 2$. If $f(x) = -10$, what is the value of $x$?
items.skill_note: Evaluating and solving are inverse tasks; here the output is known and the input must be isolated.

items.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = 7x + 7$. If $f(x) = -21$, what is the value of $x$?
choice_notes: did not divide by $7$
sign error isolating $x$
correct
added $7$ instead of subtracting it

items.stem: The table shows values of a linear function $f$: $f(1) = 8$, $f(6) = 10.5$, and $f(7) = 11$. Which equation defines $f$?
choice_notes: swapped the rate and the intercept
correct
computed the rate of change with the inputs reversed
used $f(1)$ as the intercept without adjusting for the slope
items.explanation: The rate of change is $\frac{10.5 - 8}{6 - 1} = 0.5$. Substituting $(1, 8)$ gives $0.5(1) + b = 8$, so $b = 7.5$ and $f(x) = 0.5x + 7.5$.
items.skill_note: Every table entry must satisfy the rule; the intercept is not simply the first output.

items.stem: The table shows values of a linear function $f$: $f(4) = 1$, $f(9) = -9$, and $f(10) = -11$. Which equation defines $f$?
choice_notes: used $f(4)$ as the intercept without adjusting for the slope
computed the rate of change with the inputs reversed
swapped the rate and the intercept
correct
items.explanation: The rate of change is $\frac{-9 - 1}{9 - 4} = -2$. Substituting $(4, 1)$ gives $-2(4) + b = 1$, so $b = 9$ and $f(x) = -2x + 9$.
items.skill_note: Every table entry must satisfy the rule; the intercept is not simply the first output.

items.stem: The table shows values of a linear function $f$: $f(5) = 15$, $f(7) = 25$, and $f(9) = 35$. Which equation defines $f$?
choice_notes: computed the rate of change with the inputs reversed
used $f(5)$ as the intercept without adjusting for the slope
swapped the rate and the intercept
correct
items.explanation: The rate of change is $\frac{25 - 15}{7 - 5} = 5$. Substituting $(5, 15)$ gives $5(5) + b = 15$, so $b = -10$ and $f(x) = 5x - 10$.
items.skill_note: Every table entry must satisfy the rule; the intercept is not simply the first output.

items.stem: The functions $f$ and $g$ are defined by $f(x) = 3x + 7$ and $g(x) = 3x - 7$. Which expression is equal to $f(g(x))$?
choice_notes: added the two functions instead of composing them
correct
dropped the constant $7$ after substituting
multiplied the constants instead of distributing $3$
items.explanation: Substitute $g(x)$ into $f$: $f(g(x)) = 3(3x - 7) + 7 = 9x - 21 + 7 = 9x - 14$. The slope is the product of the two slopes, and the constant is $3(-7) + 7 = -14$.
items.skill_note: Composition is not multiplication: the outer function acts on the entire inner expression.

items.stem: The functions $f$ and $g$ are defined by $f(x) = 3x + 2$ and $g(x) = 2x - 1$. Which expression is equal to $f(g(x))$?
choice_notes: dropped the constant $2$ after substituting
correct
multiplied the constants instead of distributing $3$
added the two functions instead of composing them
items.explanation: Substitute $g(x)$ into $f$: $f(g(x)) = 3(2x - 1) + 2 = 6x - 3 + 2 = 6x - 1$. The slope is the product of the two slopes, and the constant is $3(-1) + 2 = -1$.
items.skill_note: Composition is not multiplication: the outer function acts on the entire inner expression.

items.stem: A delivery van is $142$ miles from its depot and drives toward the depot at a constant speed of $40$ miles per hour. After how many hours will the van be $22$ miles from the depot?
choice_notes: correct
made an off-by-one error after dividing
solved for the time to reach the depot entirely
used only the remaining distance
items.explanation: The van must cover $142 - 22 = 120$ miles. At $40$ miles per hour, the time is $\frac{120}{40} = 3$ hours.
items.skill_note: Distance still to travel is the difference; dividing that by the rate gives the time, not dividing the total.

items.stem: A delivery van is $264$ miles from its depot and drives toward the depot at a constant speed of $60$ miles per hour. After how many hours will the van be $24$ miles from the depot?
choice_notes: solved for the time to reach the depot entirely
added the remaining distance instead of subtracting it
correct
used only the remaining distance
items.explanation: The van must cover $264 - 24 = 240$ miles. At $60$ miles per hour, the time is $\frac{240}{60} = 4$ hours.
items.skill_note: Distance still to travel is the difference; dividing that by the rate gives the time, not dividing the total.

items.stem: A delivery van is $141$ miles from its depot and drives toward the depot at a constant speed of $43$ miles per hour. After how many hours will the van be $12$ miles from the depot?
items.explanation: The van must cover $141 - 12 = 129$ miles. At $43$ miles per hour, the time is $\frac{129}{43} = 3$ hours.
items.skill_note: Distance still to travel is the difference; dividing that by the rate gives the time, not dividing the total.

items.stem: A bike rental shop charges a flat rental fee of $22$ dollars plus $4$ dollars for each hour of riding. The total cost $C$, in dollars, for $x$ hours is given by $C = 4x + 22$. What does $22$ represent in this model?
choices: the cost of each additional hour
the number of hours at which the cost is $4$ dollars
the rental fee, charged even when $x = 0$
choice_notes: described the coefficient instead of the constant
attached the constant's value to the wrong quantity
solved a cost equation that the model does not describe
correct
items.explanation: Setting $x = 0$ gives $C = 22$, so the constant is the rental fee paid before any hour is used. The coefficient $4$ is the charge per hour.
items.skill_note: The constant term is the value of the model at zero input, not the per-unit rate.

items.stem: A bike rental shop charges a flat rental fee of $15$ dollars plus $9$ dollars for each hour of riding. The total cost $C$, in dollars, for $x$ hours is given by $C = 9x + 15$. What does $15$ represent in this model?

choice_notes: correct

described the coefficient instead of the constant

items.skill_note: The constant term is the value of the model at zero input, not the per-unit rate.

items.stem: A workshop makes phone stands that sell for $13$ dollars each. The materials cost $11$ dollars per stand, and the workshop also pays $120$ dollars in fixed equipment costs. How many stands must the workshop sell to break even?
items.explanation: Break-even means revenue equals cost: $13x = 11x + 120$. So $2x = 120$ and $x = 60$.
items.skill_note: Break-even is the intersection of revenue and cost; the profit per unit is the denominator.

items.stem: A workshop makes phone stands that sell for $19$ dollars each. The materials cost $15$ dollars per stand, and the workshop also pays $72$ dollars in fixed equipment costs. How many stands must the workshop sell to break even?
choice_notes: subtracted costs instead of dividing the fixed cost
correct
rounded up instead of solving the equation exactly
ignored the per-unit material cost
items.explanation: Break-even means revenue equals cost: $19x = 15x + 72$. So $4x = 72$ and $x = 18$.
items.skill_note: Break-even is the intersection of revenue and cost; the profit per unit is the denominator.

items.stem: A workshop makes phone stands that sell for $13$ dollars each. The materials cost $10$ dollars per stand, and the workshop also pays $135$ dollars in fixed equipment costs. How many stands must the workshop sell to break even?

items.stem: A workshop makes phone stands that sell for $16$ dollars each. The materials cost $13$ dollars per stand, and the workshop also pays $156$ dollars in fixed equipment costs. How many stands must the workshop sell to break even?

items.skill_note: Break-even is the intersection of revenue and cost; the profit per unit is the denominator.

items.stem: Farid is $3$ times as old as her son. In $5$ years, she will be $2$ times as old as her son. How old is her son now?
choice_notes: correct
gave the son's age in $5$ years
subtracted the years instead of adding them
gave the mother's current age
items.explanation: Let $s$ be the son's age. Then $3s + 5 = 2(s + 5)$, so $s = 5$ and $s = 5$.
items.skill_note: Both people age by the same amount; the multiplier applies to the future ages, not the current ones.

items.stem: Maya is $3$ times as old as her son. In $8$ years, she will be $2$ times as old as her son. How old is her son now?
